\means{A lesson: an example to run, what each line does, and a task.}
\eg{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}lesson(1)}}
\field{Options}{\code{number=}, \code{solutions=}}
\field{Underneath}{simplydata's own: the lessons are written in simplydata (learn.py) and printed in plain Python; nothing is computed.}
\field{See also}{\hyperref[dict:show-packages-used]{\code{show\_\allowbreak{}packages\_\allowbreak{}used}}, \hyperref[dict:show-all-words]{\code{show\_\allowbreak{}all\_\allowbreak{}words}}, \hyperref[dict:help]{\code{help}}}
\where{Manual \manualpage{word:sdata.show-lesson}{932}{section*.663}}
\headword{show\_packages\_used}{dict:show-packages-used}
\sense{sdata}{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}packages\_\allowbreak{}used()}}
\means{List the packages that did the work behind your simplydata words, and how to cite them.}
\eg{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}packages\_\allowbreak{}used()}}
\field{Options}{\code{save\_\allowbreak{}as=}, \code{at\_\allowbreak{}end=}}
\field{Other tools}{\code{bibtex}, \code{citation}, \code{citations}, \code{cite}, \code{cite\_\allowbreak{}packages}, \code{references}, \code{session\_\allowbreak{}info}, \code{sessionInfo}}
\field{Underneath}{simplydata's own: it notes which packages its words called, reads their versions from the installed metadata (Python's importlib.metadata; R's \code{packageVersion()} and \code{citation()} through rpy2 for R packages) and prints each reference with a sentence for your methods. No data are worked on; \code{importlib.\allowbreak{}metadata.\allowbreak{}version(\textquotedbl{}pandas\textquotedbl{})} gives one version yourself.}
\field{See also}{\hyperref[dict:show-lesson]{\code{show\_\allowbreak{}lesson}}, \hyperref[dict:show-all-words]{\code{show\_\allowbreak{}all\_\allowbreak{}words}}, \hyperref[dict:help]{\code{help}}}
\where{Manual \manualpage{word:sdata.show-packages-used}{932}{section*.664}}
\headword{show\_parameters}{dict:show-parameters}
\sense{distribution}{\code{distribution.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}parameters()}}
\means{The parameters as a dictionary of plain names: \{\code{\textquotedbl{}average\textquotedbl{}}: 50, \code{\textquotedbl{}standard\_\allowbreak{}deviation\textquotedbl{}}: 10\}.}
\eg{\code{distribution.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}parameters()}}
\field{Options}{none}
\field{Underneath}{simplydata's own: it gives back the parameters as a Python dictionary of plain names, \{\code{\textquotedbl{}average\textquotedbl{}}: 50.0, \code{\textquotedbl{}standard\_\allowbreak{}deviation\textquotedbl{}}: 10.0\}; SciPy keeps them as args and kwds (loc, scale).}
\field{See also}{\hyperref[dict:show-summary]{\code{show\_\allowbreak{}summary}}, \hyperref[dict:turn-into-table]{\code{turn\_\allowbreak{}into\_\allowbreak{}table}}, \hyperref[dict:draw-chart]{\code{draw\_\allowbreak{}chart}}, \hyperref[dict:make-random-numbers]{\code{make\_\allowbreak{}random\_\allowbreak{}numbers}}, \hyperref[dict:find-variance]{\code{find\_\allowbreak{}variance}}}
\where{Manual \manualpage{word:dist.show-parameters}{635}{section*.362}}

\sense{table}{\code{table.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}rows\_\allowbreak{}that\_\allowbreak{}pull\_\allowbreak{}model()}}
\means{Show the rows that change a model from \code{explain()} the most (the table does not change).}
\eg{\code{table.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}rows\_\allowbreak{}that\_\allowbreak{}pull\_\allowbreak{}model(\textquotedbl{}marks\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} using=[\textquotedbl{}hours\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} \textquotedbl{}breakfast\textquotedbl{}])}}

\field{Other tools}{\code{cooks\_\allowbreak{}distance}, \code{influence}, \code{influence\_\allowbreak{}measures}, \code{outlier\_\allowbreak{}test}, \code{show\_\allowbreak{}influential\_\allowbreak{}rows}}
\field{Underneath}{statsmodels \code{OLS().\allowbreak{}fit()}, \code{add\_\allowbreak{}constant()}, \code{OLSInfluence()}, \code{argsort()}, \code{DataFrame()}, \code{index.\allowbreak{}to\_\allowbreak{}numpy()}}
\field{See also}{\hyperref[dict:check-model-of]{\code{check\_\allowbreak{}model\_\allowbreak{}of}}, \hyperref[dict:compare-models]{\code{compare\_\allowbreak{}models}}, \hyperref[dict:find-model-averages-of]{\code{find\_\allowbreak{}model\_\allowbreak{}averages\_\allowbreak{}of}}, \hyperref[dict:find-columns-that-predict]{\code{find\_\allowbreak{}columns\_\allowbreak{}that\_\allowbreak{}predict}}, \hyperref[dict:add-predicted-column]{\code{add\_\allowbreak{}predicted\_\allowbreak{}column}}}
\where{Manual \manualpage{word:table.show-rows-that-pull-model}{657}{section*.368}; lesson 21 (\manualpage{lesson:21}{138}{chapter.II.21}), lesson 27 (\manualpage{lesson:27}{176}{chapter.II.27})}

\field{Options}{\code{columns=}}
\field{Other tools}{\code{cases}, \code{incomplete\_\allowbreak{}cases}, \code{show\_\allowbreak{}missing}}

\where{Manual \manualpage{word:table.show-rows-with-empty-cells-in}{476}{section*.220}}

\where{Manual \manualpage{word:table.show-rows-with-outliers}{463}{section*.207}; lesson 14 (\manualpage{lesson:14}{94}{chapter.II.14})}

\headword{show\_steps}{dict:show-steps}

\sense{numbers}{\code{numbers.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}steps()}}
\means{List every step you did, in order.}
\eg{\code{numbers.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}steps()}}
\field{Options}{none}
\field{Underneath}{simplydata's own: it writes down each step as you do it and lists them. A NumPy array keeps no list of steps; your script is the record.}

\sense{distribution}{\code{distribution.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}summary()}}

\field{Underneath}{SciPy \code{gamma()}, \code{stats()}, \code{support()}, \code{median()}, \code{sqrt()}, \code{entropy()}}

\headword{show\_today}{dict:show-today}
\sense{sdata}{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}today()}}
\means{Show today's day of the 30 days of simplydata: warm-up questions, what to do and a task.}
\eg{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}today()}}
\field{Options}{\code{follow\_\allowbreak{}calendar=}}
\field{Other tools}{\code{course}, \code{tutorial}}
\field{Underneath}{simplydata's own: the 30 days are written in simplydata (\code{learn\_\allowbreak{}days}.py) and printed in plain Python; the day you reached is kept in a small JSON file on this computer (json, pathlib), and nothing is computed or sent anywhere.}
\field{See also}{\hyperref[dict:show-day]{\code{show\_\allowbreak{}day}}, \hyperref[dict:show-answers]{\code{show\_\allowbreak{}answers}}, \hyperref[dict:start-30-days]{\code{start\_\allowbreak{}30\_\allowbreak{}days}}, \hyperref[dict:go-to-next-day]{\code{go\_\allowbreak{}to\_\allowbreak{}next\_\allowbreak{}day}}}

\headword{show\_whats\_inside}{dict:show-whats-inside}
\sense{sdata}{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}whats\_\allowbreak{}inside()}}
\means{Show what a file holds without loading its numbers: its variables, directions, sizes and units.}
\eg{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}whats\_\allowbreak{}inside(\textquotedbl{}sst\_\allowbreak{}monthly.\allowbreak{}nc\textquotedbl{})}}
\field{Options}{\code{file\_\allowbreak{}name=}}
\field{Other tools}{\code{ncdisp}, \code{ncdump}, \code{ncinfo}}
\field{Underneath}{It only reads and prints what a file holds: for a netCDF file the names, directions, sizes, units and labels that xarray's \code{open\_\allowbreak{}dataset(path)} reads without loading the numbers (\code{print(ds)} shows the same facts); for .npz and .npy NumPy's np.lib.format header readers; for \code{.\allowbreak{}xlsx} openpyxl's sheet sizes. Nothing is worked out.}
\field{See also}{\hyperref[dict:save]{\code{save}}}
\where{Manual \manualpage{word:sdata.show-whats-inside}{901}{section*.620}; lesson 13 (\manualpage{lesson:13}{86}{chapter.II.13})}
\headword{show\_when\_pointing}{dict:show-when-pointing}
\sense{chart}{\code{chart.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}when\_\allowbreak{}pointing()}}
\means{The columns shown when the pointer rests on a dot or a line in a web page.}
\eg{\code{chart.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}when\_\allowbreak{}pointing(\textquotedbl{}name\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} \textquotedbl{}class\textquotedbl{})}}
\field{Options}{\code{columns.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}.\allowbreak{}}, \code{all\_\allowbreak{}lines=}}
\field{Other tools}{\code{hover}, \code{hover\_\allowbreak{}data}, \code{hover\_\allowbreak{}name}, \code{hovertemplate}, \code{mplcursors}, \code{on\_\allowbreak{}hover}, \code{show\_\allowbreak{}on\_\allowbreak{}hover}, \code{tooltip}, \code{tooltips}}
\field{Underneath}{simplydata's own: the chart is drawn by matplotlib and seaborn, as for a picture, and what they drew (the numbers of \code{get\_\allowbreak{}numbers\_\allowbreak{}drawn()}, the words of \code{get\_\allowbreak{}text\_\allowbreak{}drawn()}, the scales of \code{get\_\allowbreak{}scales\_\allowbreak{}drawn()}) is copied into a plotly figure, which nothing works out again. The columns you name go into each mark's hover text (plotly's text and hovertemplate, the job of \code{hover\_\allowbreak{}data} in plotly express); each dot's row is found by its x and y; \code{all\_\allowbreak{}lines=True} is plotly's \code{hovermode=\textquotedbl{}x unified\textquotedbl{}}.}
\field{See also}{\hyperref[dict:show-in-web-page]{\code{show\_\allowbreak{}in\_\allowbreak{}web\_\allowbreak{}page}}, \hyperref[dict:add-range-bar-x]{\code{add\_\allowbreak{}range\_\allowbreak{}bar\_\allowbreak{}x}}}
\where{Manual \manualpage{word:show-when-pointing}{413}{section*.155}; lesson 8 (\manualpage{lesson:8}{51}{chapter.II.8})}

\field{Underneath}{SciPy \code{gaussian\_\allowbreak{}filter()}}
\field{See also}{\hyperref[dict:change-size-to]{\code{change\_\allowbreak{}size\_\allowbreak{}to}}, \hyperref[dict:turn-into-change-from-average]{\code{turn\_\allowbreak{}into\_\allowbreak{}change\_\allowbreak{}from\_\allowbreak{}average}}, \hyperref[dict:get-numbers-nearest-to]{\code{get\_\allowbreak{}numbers\_\allowbreak{}nearest\_\allowbreak{}to}}, \hyperref[dict:find-values-at]{\code{find\_\allowbreak{}values\_\allowbreak{}at}}, \hyperref[dict:add-labels-to]{\code{add\_\allowbreak{}labels\_\allowbreak{}to}}}
\where{Manual \manualpage{word:grid.smooth}{910}{section*.630}}
\sense{block}{\code{block.\allowbreak{}smooth()}}

\field{Other tools}{\code{conv2}, \code{convolve2d}, \code{focal}, \code{gaussian\_\allowbreak{}filter}, \code{imgaussfilt}, \code{medfilt2}, \code{median\_\allowbreak{}filter}, \code{rolling}, \code{uniform\_\allowbreak{}filter}}
\field{Underneath}{SciPy \code{arange().\allowbreak{}reshape()}, \code{DataArray()}, \code{date\_\allowbreak{}range()}, \code{uniform\_\allowbreak{}filter()}}
\field{See also}{\hyperref[dict:turn-into-change-from-average]{\code{turn\_\allowbreak{}into\_\allowbreak{}change\_\allowbreak{}from\_\allowbreak{}average}}, \hyperref[dict:change-size-to]{\code{change\_\allowbreak{}size\_\allowbreak{}to}}, \hyperref[dict:get-numbers-nearest-to]{\code{get\_\allowbreak{}numbers\_\allowbreak{}nearest\_\allowbreak{}to}}, \hyperref[dict:find-values-at]{\code{find\_\allowbreak{}values\_\allowbreak{}at}}, \hyperref[dict:add-labels-to]{\code{add\_\allowbreak{}labels\_\allowbreak{}to}}}

\headword{undo}{dict:undo}
\sense{table}{\code{table.\allowbreak{}undo()}}
\means{Take the last step back.}
\eg{\code{table.\allowbreak{}undo()}}
\field{Options}{none}
\field{Underneath}{simplydata's own: it keeps the table as it was before each step and puts back the last one. In pandas or Polars you keep a copy yourself before a step (before = \code{df.\allowbreak{}copy()}) and go back to it.}
\field{See also}{\hyperref[dict:show-steps]{\code{show\_\allowbreak{}steps}}, \hyperref[dict:start-again]{\code{start\_\allowbreak{}again}}, \hyperref[dict:save]{\code{save}}, \hyperref[dict:make-copy]{\code{make\_\allowbreak{}copy}}, \hyperref[dict:start-chart]{\code{start\_\allowbreak{}chart}}}
\where{Manual \manualpage{word:table.undo}{802}{section*.470}; lesson 10 (\manualpage{lesson:10}{66}{chapter.II.10})}
\sense{chart}{\code{chart.\allowbreak{}undo()}}
\means{Take the last step back.}
\eg{\code{chart.\allowbreak{}undo()}}
\field{Options}{none}
\field{Underneath}{simplydata's own: a chart is a list of steps drawn only when it is shown or saved, so undo takes the last word's steps and settings back before anything is drawn again. In matplotlib you would draw the chart again without that line.}
\field{See also}{\hyperref[dict:get-size]{\code{get\_\allowbreak{}size}}, \hyperref[dict:get-scales-drawn]{\code{get\_\allowbreak{}scales\_\allowbreak{}drawn}}, \hyperref[dict:get-text-drawn]{\code{get\_\allowbreak{}text\_\allowbreak{}drawn}}, \hyperref[dict:get-numbers-drawn]{\code{get\_\allowbreak{}numbers\_\allowbreak{}drawn}}, \hyperref[dict:save]{\code{save}}}
\where{Manual \manualpage{word:undo}{238}{section*.23}}
\sense{numbers}{\code{numbers.\allowbreak{}undo()}}
\means{Take the last step back.}
\eg{\code{numbers.\allowbreak{}undo()}}
\field{Options}{none}
\field{Underneath}{simplydata's own: it keeps the numbers as they were before each step (up to 30 steps) and puts back the last one. With NumPy you keep a copy yourself before a step (before = \code{values.\allowbreak{}copy()}).}
\field{See also}{\hyperref[dict:show-steps]{\code{show\_\allowbreak{}steps}}, \hyperref[dict:start-again]{\code{start\_\allowbreak{}again}}, \hyperref[dict:turn-into-table]{\code{turn\_\allowbreak{}into\_\allowbreak{}table}}, \hyperref[dict:start-chart]{\code{start\_\allowbreak{}chart}}, \hyperref[dict:save]{\code{save}}}
\where{Manual \manualpage{word:nums.undo}{862}{section*.557}; lesson 13 (\manualpage{lesson:13}{86}{chapter.II.13})}
\sense{formula}{\code{formula.\allowbreak{}undo()}}
\means{Take the last change of the formula back.}
\eg{\code{formula.\allowbreak{}undo()}}
\field{Options}{none}
\field{Underneath}{simplydata's own: a formula keeps its earlier forms. A SymPy expression never changes, so in SymPy you keep the old one in a variable yourself.}
\field{See also}{\hyperref[dict:find-taylor-series]{\code{find\_\allowbreak{}taylor\_\allowbreak{}series}}, \hyperref[dict:show-as-decimal]{\code{show\_\allowbreak{}as\_\allowbreak{}decimal}}, \hyperref[dict:find-limit-as]{\code{find\_\allowbreak{}limit\_\allowbreak{}as}}, \hyperref[dict:group-by-powers-of]{\code{group\_\allowbreak{}by\_\allowbreak{}powers\_\allowbreak{}of}}, \hyperref[dict:show-as-latex]{\code{show\_\allowbreak{}as\_\allowbreak{}latex}}}
\where{Manual \manualpage{word:f.undo}{608}{section*.328}}

\clearpage\section*{Coming from another tool?}\label{other:names}
Names from pandas, Polars, R, NumPy, SciPy, matplotlib and seaborn, and everyday maths words. In simplydata they never run: \code{sdata.\allowbreak{}help(\textquotedbl{}groupby\textquotedbl{})} (or typing \code{table.\allowbreak{}groupby()}) points to the simplydata word. Here each name points to the word and the manual page that explains it. A name that is also a simplydata word is written with its object in front, such as \code{table.\allowbreak{}table}.
